issue.title: Plugin page options are capped at 64 KiB, and a page has no other write channel
issue.body:
# Plugin page options are capped at 64 KiB, and a page has no other write channel

**magpie 0.1.3302, Windows 11, app window (not magpie web).**

## What happens

`POST /api/plugin-pages/options` reads its body through a hard 64 KiB reader:

```go
// internal/gui/pluginpage.go:472
if err := json.NewDecoder(http.MaxBytesReader(rw, r.Body, 64<<10)).Decode(&in); err != nil {
    fail(rw, err)
    return
}
```

Above that the host answers `http: request body too large` (Go's own wording), which the window relays to the page as an error. `POST /api/plugin-pages/read` has the same cap at `pluginpage.go:443`.

## Why it stops a feature dead

A plugin page runs sandboxed: `allow-scripts`, `default-src 'none'`, no filesystem, no network. The only reads it can make are the fixed names in `pageRead` (`providers:list`, `usage:summary`, …), and it cannot reach magpie's API itself — everything goes through the window, which answers `hello` / `theme` / `options.get` / `options.set` / `read`.

So `options.set` is a page's **only** persistent write, and 64 KiB is the whole of a plugin's state.

Concretely, the case that hit this: a middleware that injects a per-client system prompt, configured from a page. One client's prompt is ~40 KB of prose. Two clients is 80 KB and the configuration can never be saved — the page cannot write it by any route, and the only way to find out is Go's error string.

`magpie plugin options <name> <json>` does write without a body, but on Windows the command line caps at 32,767 characters, so that isn't a route either.

## How it was worked around

Deflate the prompt (`CompressionStream('deflate-raw')`, stored as `{"$z": "<base64>"}`), keep a prompt shared by two clients once, and inflate it in the middleware — with its own RFC 1951 decoder, because moejs has `node:fs` / `node:buffer` / `node:glob` but no `zlib`.

That turned 143,695 characters into 40,267 and the save works. It is also ~2.2× and no more: the ceiling is still ~120 KB of text, so a third ~40 KB prompt breaks it again. A plugin should not have to ship an inflater to store its own configuration.

## What would fix it

Any one of these:

1. **Raise the cap** for `plugin-pages/options` — 1–4 MiB is nothing next to a JSON POST anywhere else in the app, and it would make the 64 KiB a non-issue for every plugin.
2. **Make it a documented limit** with a distinct error code (not bare Go text), so a page can say what happened instead of showing a server string.
3. **Give a page a document channel**: a body-free upload, or a directory under the plugin's own folder that a page may read and write. The hook already runs with `node:fs`; the page has nothing.

## Reproduction

Any plugin page whose `magpie.options.set` payload exceeds 65,536 bytes:

```js
// in a plugin page
await magpie.options.set({ blob: 'a'.repeat(70000) })
// → Error: http: request body too large
```

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5688-plugin-page-options-limit), commit [22c07066c](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/22c07066c65cc2a4e8cc016bdde13e2f4420bc1c), based on `ed0ab567`.

`POST /api/plugin-pages/options` now allows a **1 MiB whole JSON request**, including the spec and envelope. An oversized request returns HTTP 413 with code `options_too_large`. The unrelated page-read limit remains 64 KiB; 1 MiB is a bounded choice rather than unlimited storage.

The real HTTP regression fails at 70 KiB on the base. It now saves and reloads both 70 KiB and a near-limit value, verifies `plugins.json`, calls `plugin.Restart()` and checks the complete value returned over HTTP; over-limit requests have a distinct error. Parent page/panel tests passed under `-race`; GUI vet and the full offline `nogui` build passed. The test does not launch an actual Bun host, and the full test suite was not run. AI-assisted implementation and review.
